accepted_claims: For all integers k>=2 the explicitly defined graph is finite, simple, directed, and unit-edge-cost with k distinct ordered terminals.
Its exact integral optimum is C_k-k^2, where C_k=sum_{l=1}^k (k-l+1)floor(k/l).
A feasible vector for the original edge path-distance LP has objective C_k/3.
Its actual gaps have liminf at least 3.
not_accepted_as_proved: Solution of the original constant-versus-unbounded question

prior_packaging_correction.authorship: Independent audit, not the original proof author
prior_packaging_correction.scope: Inventory checker only, with regenerated integrity metadata; mathematical proof, source records and mathematical certificates unchanged

exact_original_target: The edge-cardinality directed linear-k-cut distance LP has an absolute integrality-gap bound for all k, or admits an unbounded-gap family.
lower_bound_limit: The lower bounds 3(1-k^2/C_k) tend to 3. The actual gaps have liminf at least 3; convergence of actual gaps to 3 is not proved.
publication_edition: Authored proof-only accepted partial; no new mathematical correction.
